destination.name: Kinchega National Park
destination.tagline: An outback national park on the Darling River with lake birdlife and an old woolshed.
destination.description: Kinchega National Park covers 44,259 hectares on the Darling River beside the town of Menindee, 111 km south-east of Broken Hill. NPWS describes river red gums rising from the water of the Menindee lake system, with a wide array of birdlife. The park's woolshed dates from 1875, and six million sheep were sheared there in 97 years. The park is managed with the Menindee Aboriginal Elders Council under a joint management program.
whyVisit: Spot birdlife among river red gums

goodToKnow.title: Entry fee in coins
goodToKnow.detail: Park entry is 8 dollars per vehicle per day, paid by envelope at a pay-and-display point, so bring the correct coins.

goodToKnow.title: Lakes may be low
goodToKnow.detail: The Menindee Lakes fill only after months of rain in southern Queensland, so check conditions before planning around the water.

goodToKnow.title: Woolshed tours are seasonal
goodToKnow.detail: Woolshed tours run in Easter, winter and spring school holidays; the park itself is open daily.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Summers here are hot semi-arid, so the cooler months, {months}, suit camping and walking; woolshed tours run in Easter, winter and spring school holidays.
